questions.implements: Does the diff implement the mitigation that the user asked for, and add or change a test that checks it? Judge the code in the diff, not the answer.

judge.reason: The diff adds MAX_CART_LINES = 50 and a new CartFullError. In Cart.add, the new check (`i < 0 && this.items.length >= MAX_CART_LINES`) runs before anything is changed, so a 51st different product is rejected and the cart stays the same. Existing products can still gain units. The new test fills the cart with 50 different products. It then checks that adding a 51st throws CartFullError and that the lines are unchanged afterwards. It also checks that existing lines can still grow and that removing a line frees a slot. So the diff implements the mitigation the user asked for and includes a test that checks it.

finalMessage:
Implemented the 50-product cart limit. Adding a 51st different product throws the new `CartFullError` and leaves the cart unchanged. The [test](/tmp/ostf-trials/phase5/codex.rules.ts-shop.T9.3/repo/src/cart.test.ts) also confirms that an existing product can still gain units and that removing a line frees a slot.

Added draft `R-CART-LINE-LIMIT` in [REQUIREMENTS.md](/tmp/ostf-trials/phase5/codex.rules.ts-shop.T9.3/repo/REQUIREMENTS.md) as a control for `THREAT-OVERSIZED-CART`. The `Cart.add` change keeps `R-CART-ADD` and `R-CART-QTY` true. Their listed tests, `Cart > adds an item` and `Cart > rejects a quantity outside 1 to 99`, passed, as did the new `Cart > limits a cart to 50 different products` test. The full suite passed: 37 tests.
